# Go Bag getting started

You keep the owner's bot team recoverable: one Go Bag document that can rebuild every bot on any platform, refreshed weekly and backed up to Google Drive. Greet the owner in one line, then ask these one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. Which bots do you have, and which one is the Chief of Staff (the one that keeps the Go Bag)?
2. What timezone should timestamps and schedules use, and which day and time should the weekly refresh run (full hours; the backup runs one hour later)?
3. Is your Google Drive connected? If not, help connect it.
4. Do you have a rulebook Page or document every bot follows? If so, where?
5. Which secrets or logins exist (names only, never values), and where do you keep your 2FA recovery codes (location only)?
Then: create the working folder with bots, REQUEST.txt, team.md and build.py from the skill "Grok Bot team Go Bag and external backup", create the two weekly routines, ask every bot to write its file, run the first build, upload to the Drive folders, and show the owner the result. Offer a tabletop restore drill and say a second backup location is an optional later upgrade.

# Grok Bot team Go Bag and external backup

Goal: one portable document with everything needed to recreate every bot on another platform, rebuilt on a schedule, plus timestamped copies of it and of the team rulebook in Google Drive (the external backup). Never put secrets in it: name env vars and secret references, never values.

## Layout on the shared computer (folder `GOBAG`)
- `GOBAG/bots/<BotName>.md`: one spec per bot, written by the bot itself
- `GOBAG/REQUEST.txt`: the instruction every bot follows (template below)
- `GOBAG/team.md`: team-level sections, written by the Chief of Staff
- `GOBAG/Rulebook.md`: Markdown export of the rulebook Page, if one exists
- `GOBAG/build.py`: assembles and checks everything
- `GOBAG/out/`: timestamped builds. Make `GOBAG/bots` writable by all bots.

## Per-bot template (REQUEST.txt asks for these exact headings so the check can verify them)
Header: `# <Name> · <Role>` then `schema_version | bot_id | generated_at (with timezone) | go_bag_version`.
1. Identity: name, role, purpose, tone.
2. Standing instructions: the full system prompt, faithful, not summarised, including never-do rules.
3. Routines: name, cron, IANA timezone, active or paused, overlap, retry and missed-run behaviour, and the full saved prompt.
4. Model and tool permissions: model or provider settings if known, tools allowed, needing approval, forbidden.
5. Connectors and MCP: name, endpoint and transport if known, scopes, login name only, secret reference (name only).
6. Skills and files owned, with paths.
7. Pages, report formats, chat message format, data stores.
8. Key memory: lasting facts, tracked lists, thresholds, and how memory can be exported.
9. Dependencies and run order, and recovery tier (1 = restore first, 3 = last).
10. Known failures and workarounds: impact, cause, fix.
11. Platform mapping notes: which platform features it relies on and what the new platform needs instead.
12. Changelog: date and what changed.
On refreshes a bot rewrites its file only if something changed, and adds a changelog line.

## Team sections (`team.md`, kept by the Chief of Staff)
Version and changelog; recovery objectives and tiers; dependency graph and run order; restore procedure in three phases (activate, recover tier by tier, reconstitute secrets and verify, with one successful manual run per bot); restore drill log (tabletop first, then yearly); secrets inventory (name, where stored, who uses it, owner, rotation steps, never values); leaked-secret runbook (revoke at the issuer, check logs, rotate, tell the owner); accounts and ownership, naming only where 2FA recovery codes are kept; precedence rule (owner's latest instruction, then rulebook, then bot instructions); shared data stores; platform glossary; backup policy. Write "not recorded" for anything unknown.

## Step 1. Collect specs
Send each task bot a wake-up message (priority true) to read REQUEST.txt and write its file, replying only "Go Bag file written" (or "No change" on refreshes). The Chief of Staff writes its own file the same way.

## Step 2. Export the rulebook
Convert the rulebook Page faithfully to `Rulebook.md`, then spot-check it.

## Step 3. Build and check
Run `python3 GOBAG/build.py`. It writes `out/Bot_Go_Bag_<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM>.md` plus a `.sha256` file, prints PROBLEMS and exits 1 if any bot file lacks sections 1 to 12 or looks like it holds a secret. Fix and rebuild; never upload a failed build. The script assembles: how to recreate, the team section, a roster, each bot file, the rulebook, and a completeness check; it checks sections with a regex per number 1 to 12, scans for private keys and password/token/secret/api key assignments, writes the sha256 sidecar, and exits 1 on problems. Set its timezone constant to the owner's timezone.

## Step 4. Page index (optional)
Keep one reusable Page, edited each run, with the roster, last refresh and backup times, and the latest Drive links.

## Step 5. Google Drive backup, tidy and timestamped
Folders (create once, look up by name first, never duplicate): `Bot Backups / Go Bag /` holds `Bot_Go_Bag_<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM>.md` and its `.sha256`; `Bot Backups / Bot Rulebook /` holds `Bot_Rulebook_<YYYY-MM-DD_HHMM>.md`. Timestamp in the file name in the owner's timezone; folders private; upload with conversion to Google types disabled; searching by folder name can miss new folders, so also list the root and reuse folder ids; afterwards list the folders and confirm names and sizes match; never delete or overwrite old backups (propose retention such as weekly for 12 weeks then monthly, only with the owner's yes). Report the links.

## Step 6. Schedule (routines, full-hour times)
- Refresh routine, weekly: update the Chief of Staff file, wake bots to rewrite only if changed, export the rulebook, build, edit the Page.
- Backup routine, weekly, one hour later: rebuild, check, upload, verify, update the Page, one-line result with links.
Keep runs lean: one background worker.

## Good practice notes
- 3-2-1 backups: three copies, two kinds of storage, one off-site. A single Drive copy is a start; a second location is a later, optional upgrade.
- Run a tabletop restore drill when first built and yearly; log it. A backup nobody has restored from is unproven.
- Keep a changelog and version number so a restore knows which template it is reading.

## Restoring
Open the latest `Bot_Go_Bag_*` file, check its `.sha256`, follow "How to recreate" and the team section's restore procedure.
